summary: Set 112 Session 1 of 3: the router-side removal of the Lightweight tier. Deleted 5 production modules whole (dedicated_verification, external_verification, pending_verification, change_verification_mode, migrate_lightweight_to_canonical_v4 -- 2,581 lines) plus 8 test modules, and excised the in-place branches: both close-out gate blocks in close_session, the typed-session CLI surface and its two session_state writers (399 lines), runtime_mode precedence step 3, and the lightweight-to-v4 slot in the migrator chain and the shipped schema manifest. 4,404 net production lines removed; pytest 3,811 -> 3,578 tests. tier: lightweight now fails LOUD: spec_config raises LightweightTierRemovedError carrying a one-line migration message that names both remedies (tier: full plus either DABBLER_* keys or a copilot-cli seat). Prose mentions and non-canonical fences stay inert so archives, proposals and the migration notice remain readable. Beyond the spec's kill list, the session closed a verification escape it did not name: gate_checks._set_is_lightweight returned True on the DABBLER_NO_ROUTER env var ALONE and gated both check_verification_integrity and the run-of-record freshness check, so one environment variable -- no tier, no attestation, no human -- disarmed two gates. --no-router now means exactly one thing, suppress routed calls, and its self-written 'manual' attestation is gone too; --manual-verify is the only attested bypass. Three inverted regression tests pin that. Cross-provider verification (gpt-5.5, orchestrator provider anthropic excluded) found four Major defects across a 2-lens discovery fan-out and a supplementary pass; all four were accepted and fixed, none disputed. The important one: the fail-loud loader was TRUE BUT UNREACHABLE -- nothing on the start_session happy path parsed the config block, so a stranded Lightweight consumer would have been registered and written to disk before meeting an unrelated error later, and the one live caller (gate_checks._uat_policy) swallowed the error in a broad except, which would additionally have evaporated an armed UAT policy. Fixed with a spec_config.refuse_if_lightweight boundary helper called before every write in both lifecycle CLIs, a re-raise in _uat_policy, and -- from the verifier's own acceptance criterion -- support for the quoted YAML form tier: "lightweight", which the regex would have let through. Also fixed: ai_router/docs/close-out.md still documented the two deleted close gates and told operators to commit a set to Lightweight tier; and the extension's Upgrade Older Session Sets command still shelled out to the deleted migrator as step 2 of 3, which would have failed the whole bulk upgrade for every user who could click it. Remediation-review returned VERIFIED, 4 fixes accepted 0 rejected. Runs of record after the last change: pytest 3,576 passed / 0 failed / 9 skipped; Layer 3 Playwright 33 passed (required -- this session edited three blessed writers). A measured finding contradicts a spec premise and is recorded rather than smoothed over: the test matrix shrank 6.1% but CI wall clock did not move, because the deleted modules cost 3.64s of a 16-minute suite. Session 3's acceptance gate should assert zero live references, not a minutes saving.

reason.specifics: Session 2 is the other half of one decision, not a new problem. It consumes this session's kill inventory and must describe the boundary refusal built here in the wording chosen here; the Getting Started form's new first question follows directly from the tier fork this session made unreachable. Two deferrals need carrying: the generated cold-start/full fixture tree regenerates from S2's template edits (never hand-edit the golden), and docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md still documents typed sessions whose writers this session deleted.
